questions.question: The existence of atoms was confirmed by matter, electricity, and which other phenomenon?
questions.explanation: The material states matter, electricity, and radiation are atomic in character.

questions.question: Theories proposed to study the physical state of an atom from spectrum characteristics are called which of the following?
questions.explanation: These theories are called atomic models.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as an important atomic model?
questions.explanation: Thomson's atomic model is one of the important models listed.

questions.question: The first scientific explanation of atomic structure was proposed by which scientist?
questions.explanation: J. J. Thomson proposed the first scientific explanation in 1899.

questions.question: Bohr improved on the atomic model of which scientist?
questions.explanation: Bohr improved on the model by Rutherford.

questions.question: Which model is considered close to the modern atomic model?
questions.explanation: The modern atomic model is close to Bohr's atomic model.

questions.question: Which theory was applied by Bohr to revolving electrons?
questions.explanation: Bohr applied Planck's Quantum Theory to revolving electrons.

questions.question: The modern atomic model is closest to which scientist's model?
questions.explanation: The modern atomic model is close to Bohr's atomic model.

questions.question: In which year was Thomson's atomic model proposed?
questions.explanation: Thomson proposed his atomic model in 1899.

questions.question: Thomson's atomic model described the atom as a sphere filled with which substance?
questions.explanation: The atom was a sphere filled with positively charged matter.

questions.question: In Thomson's model, electrons serve to balance which charge?
questions.explanation: Electrons are embedded to balance the positive charge.

questions.question: In Thomson's model, the number of electrons is proportional to which property?
questions.explanation: The number of electrons was proportional to the atomic weight.

questions.question: Thomson postulated that electrons are held together by which force?
questions.explanation: Electrons are held by electrostatic forces of attraction.

questions.question: Which arrangement could Thomson's model not show completely?
questions.explanation: The model could not show the complete arrangement of electrons and protons.

questions.question: Thomson's model was rejected because it could not explain which spectrum?
questions.explanation: It could not explain the hydrogen spectrum completely.

questions.question: Thomson's model gave no explanation for which experimental observation?
questions.explanation: No explanation was given for large scattering of alpha particles.

questions.question: Thomson's theory today is important mainly because it did which of the following?
questions.explanation: It pioneered the way of modern research in this sphere.

questions.question: Thomson's model assumed the atom as a whole was what?
questions.explanation: From the observation that the atom as a whole was stable, he postulated electron arrangement.

questions.question: In which year was Rutherford's atomic model proposed?
questions.explanation: Rutherford proposed his atomic model in 1911.

questions.question: Rutherford's model was based on scattering of alpha particles by which material?
questions.explanation: The experiment involved scattering of alpha particles by thin metal foil.

questions.question: Which two associates conducted the alpha particle scattering experiment with Rutherford?
questions.explanation: Geiger and Marsden conducted the experiment with Rutherford.

questions.question: In Rutherford's model, the nucleus is surrounded by particles with which charge?
questions.explanation: The atom is made up of a small positive nucleus with electrons around it.

questions.question: In Rutherford's model, the total negative charge equals which charge?
questions.explanation: The total negative charge equals the concentrated positive charge in the nucleus.

questions.question: In Rutherford's model, most of the atom's volume is described as which?
questions.explanation: Such a picture leaves most of the volume unoccupied.

questions.question: Rutherford assumed that electrons revolve around the nucleus like which system?
questions.explanation: Electrons revolve around the nucleus like planets around the sun.

questions.question: In Rutherford's model, which force balances the electrostatic force of attraction?
questions.explanation: The centrifugal force due to rotation balances the electrostatic force.

questions.question: What did Rutherford assume about the state of electrons in his model?
questions.explanation: Rutherford assumed electrons were not at rest but revolved around the nucleus.

questions.question: According to electromagnetic theory, an accelerating charge must do which of the following?
questions.explanation: An accelerating charge must radiate energy as electromagnetic radiation.

questions.question: In Rutherford's model, an electron must move along which path?
questions.explanation: The electron must move along a spiral path of decreasing radius.

questions.question: According to Rutherford's model, the atom would last for which duration?
questions.explanation: The planetary system would last for an extremely short period.

questions.question: In practice, spectral lines of which type are always observed?
questions.explanation: Spectral lines of fixed wavelength are always observed.

questions.question: Which difficulty arises from a positively charged nucleus surrounded by electrons?
questions.explanation: The protons should make electrons fall into the nucleus due to electrostatic attraction.

questions.question: How did Rutherford solve the difficulty of electrons falling into the nucleus?
questions.explanation: He assumed electrons revolve around the nucleus in various orbits.

questions.question: What brings up another difficulty in Rutherford's model?
questions.explanation: A revolving electron is continuously accelerated due to change of direction.

questions.question: What is the consequence of energy loss by orbiting electrons?
questions.explanation: The electron must move along a spiral path of decreasing radius till it falls into the nucleus.

questions.question: What is in sharp contrast to the prediction that atoms would collapse?
questions.explanation: But this is in sharp contrast to the fact that atoms show no tendency to collapse.

questions.question: In which year was Bohr's atomic model proposed?
questions.explanation: Neils Bohr proposed his atomic model in 1913.

questions.question: Bohr retained which part of Rutherford's model?
questions.explanation: Bohr retained the small positively charged nucleus in the centre.

questions.question: Bohr applied which theory to revolving electrons?
questions.explanation: Bohr applied Planck's Quantum Theory to the revolving electrons.

questions.question: According to Bohr, an electron in the same orbit does which of the following?
questions.explanation: The energy of an electron remains constant so long as it stays in the same orbit.

questions.question: In Bohr's model, orbits are also known as which term?
questions.explanation: Orbits are also known as energy levels or energy shells.

questions.question: In Bohr's model, which orbit has the least energy?
questions.explanation: The smallest orbit, first from the nucleus, has the least energy.

questions.question: In Bohr's model, which orbit has the maximum energy?
questions.explanation: The farthest orbit has the maximum energy.

questions.question: Energy is emitted when an electron moves from which level?
questions.explanation: Energy is emitted when an electron moves from a higher energy level to a lower energy level.

questions.question: Energy is absorbed when an electron moves from which level?
questions.explanation: Energy is absorbed when an electron moves from a lower energy level to a higher energy level.

questions.question: Bohr postulated that angular momentum can have only which type of values?
questions.explanation: Bohr postulated that angular momentum can have only definite or discrete values.

questions.question: In Bohr's postulate, what does n represent?
questions.explanation: n is an integer representing the orbit.

questions.question: The charge of an electron is which value?
questions.explanation: The charge of an electron is 1.6 times 10 to the power minus 19 coulomb.

questions.question: The mass of an electron is which value?
questions.explanation: The mass of an electron is 9.1 times 10 to the power minus 31 kilogram.

questions.question: Bohr's atomic model cannot be applied to which type of atoms?
questions.explanation: It cannot be applied to complex atoms having two or more planetary electrons.
